decision.title: Optional features add library functions (packet 7.10a)
decision.summary: An optional feature's definition can carry library_functions, which the processor's function library serves after the registered parts, so the functions are absent (XPST0017) from programs that do not name the feature.

body.p: , after , , , . A feature whose place is "the functions are absent" (XPST0017: fn:parse-html and fn:html-doc, the EXPath Binary and File functions) must not link its rows into a program that does not name it, so its rows cannot be a library part of src/function_library_*.c (the registry links every part).

item.p: sxml_optional_feature_definition (src/optional_feature_internal.h) gains library_functions: a const sxml_native_function_view * of static const rows in the feature's own files, or NULL.

The processor's function library serves every registered XPath part, then the library_functions of each configured feature in kind order (sxml_processor_make_library_part_list in src/processor.c). The list lives in allocator memory only while the library is initialized (the library does not keep it). XQuery and XSLT chain their own tables in front of the processor's, so they see the feature's functions too.

Without the feature the functions are absent, as before: XPST0017 at compile time, false from fn:function-available, nothing from fn:function-lookup. A feature's file that holds rows names its view differently from sxml_function_library_<part>, so the CMake registry (cmake/SxmlParts.cmake) does not take it as a part.
